proposalRationale:
TJR structure-point location: a swing high/low is marked at the WICK extreme.

CLASSIFICATION: SOURCE-STATED (TJR). Evidence EV|EVSRC|TJR|20260727|002|020 is an explicit
statement, directness=direct_explicit, extractionCertainty=high. Note the verbatim excerpt is
"We take the highest point of those two candlesticks" -- it does not contain the word "wick".
The wick reading is supplied by TJR's own candle-anatomy definition in the same source,
EV|EVSRC|TJR|20260727|002|016 (certain): "The top of the top wick is the high and the bottom of
the bottom wick is the low." So "highest point" = high = upper wick tip is SOURCE-STATED, but it
is a two-step reading, not a single verbatim sentence. Flagged so the distinction is not lost.

MECHANICAL SPECIFICATION: given an ordered candle series, a swing high is formed by an up candle
at index i followed by a down candle at index i+1 (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|064); the marked level is
max(candle[i].high, candle[i+1].high). A swing low is a down candle followed by an up candle;
the marked level is min(candle[i].low, candle[i+1].low). Open/close are used only to classify a
candle as up (close>open) or down (close<open).

DATA REQUIRED: OHLC series at the working timeframe. Nothing else. No session data, no volume.

FALSIFICATION: annotate a sample of TJR's own charted examples and compare each marked level
against both candidates. If a material share of his marked levels sit at max(open,close) rather
than at the wick tip, this candidate is refuted. A single unambiguous counter-example on a candle
with a large wick is sufficient to move it to contested-within-source.

CONFLICTING EVIDENCE (already recorded, unresolved): XCONTRA|20260727|003 pairs this claim with
CLAIM|ALEX_G|20260727|020, where Alex G states the opposite for his own strategy
("So, I base my highs and lows to the bodies of the candlesticks" / "I'm placing it at the body
of that candlestick, not at the wick"). This is a CROSS-EDUCATOR disagreement, NOT evidence that
TJR is internally inconsistent: within the TJR corpus the wick reading is unanimous across
CLAIM|TJR|20260727|061, |062 and |065, with zero contradicting evidence items. The contradiction
must not be resolved by preferring one educator; it is only resolvable per-strategy.

IMPLEMENTATION CROSS-CHECK (informational, not evidence about TJR): the shipped MOGO Phase 1
engine already implements the wick reading -- findTjrSessionExtremes() ranks candles by c.h/c.l,
and each session zone spans from the body extreme (inner edge) to the wick extreme (outer edge).
Pinned by Fixtures 49-52 in tests/v123_tjr_phase1_session_zone_tests.js. The engine agreeing with
the claim is a consistency observation only; it is not independent confirmation of the claim,
since the engine was built from this same research.

UNKNOWN: (a) whether the two-candle pattern in |064 is TJR's only structure-point definition or
just a teaching simplification -- |063 states the more general "move up followed by a move down";
(b) whether the same wick rule governs BREAK detection as governs MARKING (CLAIM|TJR|20260727|015
defines a break of structure as price CLOSING beyond the level, which is a body-based test -- so
marking and breaking may deliberately use different price components; no source statement
reconciles them); (c) tie-breaking when both candles share the identical high is unstated.
